judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Flat self-introductions, a petition and a sponsorship mechanic, an odd small errand (an urchin who has aggravated the bats) and an item handed over mid-speech. Plain, a little clumsy, very Nox.

items.label: B
items.critique: The smuggler's single run-on sentence of grievance is a written comic set piece, not Nox's plain delivery. The shield's little backstory ('Never did find out whose it was') is a writer's flourish.

items.label: C
items.critique: A plain, transactional sales pitch with a big round price, 'lad', and a parting warning about the villain. It has the slightly stiff, functional exposition of Westwood's merchants.

items.label: D
items.critique: Packs too many beats into short lines: a fright gag, the lore of the lighthouse, 'mind you don't drop it', then a sinking-house punchline with a discount. Its comedy is built like a sketch, and Nox's isn't.

items.label: E
items.critique: Exasperated, chatty exposition ('It's not easy running a smuggling ring, you know'), 'Tell you what...', and a thank-you that restates the reward. Westwood's rhythm and its mild humour.

items.label: F
items.critique: The shrine plea apes Westwood's archaic register ('abominable dead', 'nefarious witch'), but the outcome says 'As I vowed... a spell' when no spell was promised, and the boatman's terse modern patter belongs to another voice.

items.label: G
items.critique: 'Here's my offer', 'Will you?', the jailer's routine laid out like a heist brief, and the 'pulled it out of the moat, nobody ever claimed it' reward lore are all tidy, crafted beats that are foreign to Nox.

items.label: H
items.critique: The buried-in-it-but-didn't-move-around-much gag and the grudging 'Took you long enough' are punchier and more knowing than Westwood's humour. The lines are compressed rather than plainly expository.

items.label: I
items.critique: 'Hello, young sir. I surmise...', double-dash punctuation, 'savage scum', and exact gold sums in the thanks. A wordy, earnest townsfolk voice that is pure Nox.

items.label: J
items.critique: Melodramatic captives, 'the menfolk cannot live without us', and a decline answered with a joke about grumbling Ogre stomachs. Westwood's broad humour and its long exclamatory sentences.

tells: New texts give rewards a little invented backstory ('found it in the moat/field, never knew whose it was'). Westwood just names the item and hands it over.
New texts compress several comic beats into short punchy lines with a sketch-like setup and punchline. Westwood's humour is broader and sits inside longer, plainer exposition.
New texts favour terse imperatives and brisk modern idiom ('Here's my offer', 'Will you?', 'If the guards ask, you never saw us'). Westwood's townsfolk ramble, explain and exclaim.
Pastiche of Westwood's archaic register sits next to a plainer voice in the same text, and outcomes do not match what the ask promised.
